messages:
lina-cs: Heads-up — multiple tickets from Acme and BetaApps reporting 502/timeout spikes hitting hosted inference in eu-central around 08:07-08:12 UTC. They see higher p95 latency and occasional auth failures. Can infra/sre take a look?

sre-oncall-bot: alert: hosted-api-eu-central elevated 5xx rate (routes /v1/generate, /v1/chat). Incident created: INC-2026-3192. p95 latency rose from ~900ms to ~3.6s.

maya-oncall: I'll triage. Lina, please paste any request IDs or sample curl payloads.

lina-cs: Provided sample header X-Req-ID=acme-20260320-1204 and attached curl from customer showing HTTP 502. They reported first error 08:07:12 UTC and intermittent failures for ~18 minutes.

kai-eng-runtime: Reproduced from our eu-central gateway:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Req-ID: acme-20260320-1204" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.example (54.93.45.21) port 443
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-request-id: acme-20260320-1204
```
Gateway is returning 502 before model layer, retries observed at proxy tier.

diego-netops: Collecting network telemetry. I'm seeing packet drop and path asymmetry between eu-central-az2 and eu-central-az3 starting ~08:05 UTC. Example mtr from our edge -> az3:
```
host to 10.240.3.12
 1. 10.0.0.1 0.6 ms
 2. 203.0.113.9 (AS64521) 5.1 ms
 3. 198.51.100.14  *  (loss)
 4. 198.51.100.22 12.8 ms
```
TCP handshake retries and TLS timeouts observed on proxy->backend connections when cross-AZ. Local AZ->AZ3 flows show ~3.5% loss at peak.

maya-oncall: Diego, does KV cache traffic (proxy->model) look impacted or is it general egress? Any auth microservice timeouts?

diego-netops: Primarily inter-AZ egress. Backend TLS handshake latency spikes correlated with KV cache miss rate increase. Auth introspection had elevated latencies for tokens validated across AZ boundary — explains the brief auth error reports.

ashwin-provider: Carrier status: We applied a partial policy change at 08:02 UTC for peering AS paths; a subsequent route-map tweak inadvertently caused asymmetric returns for a subset of prefixes into eu-central. We've rolled back the policy at 08:18 UTC (rollback ID: rb-1a9c4). Convergence window expected up to 20 minutes for some flows. Monitoring shows decreasing loss after rollback.

maya-oncall: Please share the BGP update IDs and timestamps for correlation and attach route-change diffs.

ashwin-provider: Pushed bgp-update id bgp-20260320-08:02 and rollback rb-1a9c4 at 08:18. I'll send the diffs to diego-netops and include expected AS path changes.

kai-eng-runtime: Short-term mitigations applied: 1) enabled strict AZ affinity for latency-sensitive customer routes to avoid cross-AZ backend hops where possible, 2) lowered model activation timeout threshold and enabled instant fallback to a pre-warmed smaller variant for critical keys, 3) slowed retry backoff to avoid cascading retries. We'll monitor 5xx reduction.

ops-systems: Observed token introspection queueing increased ~2x during the event — spurious auth errors were side-effects, not token revocations. No billing anomalies detected.

lina-cs: Informed Acme/BetaApps: sorry for the outage, provided temporary mitigations and ETA for provider convergence (per carrier). Customers asked whether this could recur and requested permanent safeguards.

diego-netops: Current measurements after rollback: packet loss az2->az3 dropped from peak ~4.1% to ~0.4% over 20 minutes. RTT p95 still elevated by ~90ms for ~7% of flows. Continuing to steer traffic away from affected paths.

maya-oncall: Root cause summary: transient carrier route-policy change caused asymmetric routing and packet loss across AZ boundaries -> proxy-to-backend TLS handshakes timed out -> gateway returned 502s for inference routes. Resolution: carrier rollback (rb-1a9c4), local AZ affinity, warmed fallback models, and adjusted retry behavior.

lina-cs: Customers accepted temporary fixes; they've asked for formal RCA and long-term mitigations.

diego-netops: Proposed long-term actions: enforce provider change windows with pre-checks, require providers to run route-policy dry-runs and announce planned changes, pursue multi-homing with a second transit vendor in eu-central, and implement inside-network routing logic to prefer same-AZ backends for latency SLA customers.

kai-eng-runtime: I'll push runtime changes: earlier local-fallback, AZ-aware connection pooling, and new alerts for per-AZ handshake latency >300ms. Also will add a dashboard to surface cross-AZ TLS handshake histograms.

ops-systems: We'll harden token introspection timeouts and add local cache fallback for validation to reduce cross-AZ dependency for auth.

maya-oncall: Incident declared resolved at 08:48 UTC (5xx rates back to baseline; packet loss <0.5%). Filing full incident report with pcap snippets, BGP diff, rollback ID rb-1a9c4, request IDs, and follow-up owners: diego -> provider multi-homing + SLAs, kai -> runtime changes + alerts, ops -> auth cache improvement.

lina-cs: Thank you all — I'll circulate the customer-facing RCA and schedule a postmortem meeting. :white_check_mark:
